answer: Like saffron, which is precious because each gram takes thousands of hand-picked flowers, an agent identity can require burning one scarce, non-fungible on-chain artifact to mint. The terrace of entry is a one-way burn: the artifact is destroyed, so a farm cannot share or reuse it across fake identities, and bulk-buying the fixed supply drives the price up with every fake it creates. Each identity's cost is therefore real, sunk, and unparallelizable - a farm hits the summit of what it can afford long before it can flood the network.
